summary.text: Adam Cleveland is the Democratic candidate for Georgia House of Representatives District 48 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Scott Hilton (R).
An attorney and small business owner, he says he helped write and pass three judgment-enforcement bills between 2015 and 2020.

paragraphs.text: Adam Cleveland graduated from North Springs High School, earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Georgia in 2000 and a law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2005.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was born in Atlanta, has lived in Georgia his whole life, and has been an attorney for the past 20 years and a small business owner.
He said that from 2015 through 2020 he co-wrote, testified in support of, and helped pass three bills on judgment enforcement, and that in 2025 he testified against a bill on money judgments.
He said he has served on the board of the National Creditors Bar Association and chaired his Georgia Bar section.

Cleveland's stated campaign priorities include protecting voting independence, structural reforms such as term limits, ranked choice voting and independent district maps, and expanding Medicaid in Georgia.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on May 19, 2026.
